title: sequence-length-aware-window-autoscaler and tenant burst degrade limiter
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Introduce a sequence-length-aware autoscaler that improves provisioning accuracy for variable-length workloads; adds tenant-level burst degradation limiter to reduce noisy neighbor-induced SLA violations; new telemetry exposes per-seqlen utilization breakdowns for capacity planning.
description:
Context and motivation: production inference workloads show large variation in decoded sequence lengths (short responses for embeddings/intent classification, long for summarization). Existing autoscaling uses request-count and aggregate token rates which underprovisions for long-decoding tails and overprovisions for short bursts. This PR introduces a sequence-length-aware window autoscaler (seqlen-window-autoscaler) that tracks token-decoding distributions per pool and per tenant and makes scale decisions on a time-windowed, p95 token-decoding budget. It also introduces a tenant burst degrade limiter: a soft admission controller that intentionally degrades non-critical bursts from a tenant when observed utilization cross-couples with other tenants and risks latency SLOs.

Changes in this PR (summary): - New autoscaler component: seqlen_window_autoscaler that computes decodelength histograms, estimates per-request token costs, and converts short/long mix into an effective concurrency target. - Tenant burst degrade limiter: admission policy that applies graceful tail-drop (drop-to-limited-concurrency) for bursty behavioral patterns while recording decline reason and offering automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant. - Telemetry: per-pool and per-tenant metrics for seq_len_p50/p95/p99, token_rate_by_seqbucket, effective_concurrency_estimate, and degrade_limiter_events. - API: config knobs under dedicated/autoscaling: window_size_seconds, seq_buckets (bins), pctl_target, degrade_thresholds, degrade_duration_seconds, fallback_policy. - Safety: integrate with existing provision-safety-checks to avoid decommitting capacity during sustained long-tail decoders; add a back-pressure signal to gateway routing to prefer fast-compatible model variants during degrades. - Tests: unit tests for histogram merging, end-to-end simulation in benchmark-lab with synthetic seq distributions, and integration smoke with dedicated fleet in staging.

Detailed usage notes (single-line config example): {"autoscaling":{"type":"seqlen-window","window_size_seconds":60,"seq_buckets":[0,32,128,512,2048],"pctl_target":95,"scale_up_multiplier":1.25,"degrade_thresholds":{"p95_cpu":0.85,"p95_latency_ms":1200},"degrade_duration_seconds":30}} (actual config lives under dedicated/config/autoscalers.yaml). The autoscaler operates as a replacement policy for pools that opt-in; default remains the existing token-rate autoscaler.

Commits (high-level): - a1b2c3d: initial seqlen_window_autoscaler implementation + histogram proto and merge logic - b4c5d6e: integrate autoscaler into provisioner API and add configuration plumbing - c7d8e9f: tenant burst degrade limiter + admission API and gateway backpressure hook - d0e1f2a: telemetry labels, metrics, and dashboards + unit tests - e3f4g5h: simulation harness and integration test fixes

Files changed (high-level): - dedicated/autoscaler/seqlen_window_autoscaler.go: core logic for windowing and histogram-based concurrency target - dedicated/autoscaler/histogram.proto: compact histogram message and merge helpers - gateway/admission/degrade_limiter.go: tenant burst limiter and policy enforcement - telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml: new metrics definitions and tag keys - console/dashboards/seqlen-utilization.json: new observability dashboard - benchmark-lab/simulations/seqlen_mixture_test.py: synthetic workload and validation harness - tests/autoscaler/seqlen_window_test.go: unit test matrix

Small illustrative snippet (autoscaler decision, pseudo-code): "if p95_estimated_token_rate > provision_capacity * safety_margin then signal_scale_up() else if bursty_tenant && degrade_limiter.ShouldDegrade(tenant) then apply_graceful_degrade(tenant)". This is intentionally high-level; see dedicated/autoscaler/seqlen_window_autoscaler.go for exact thresholds and smoothing constants.

Review timeline and conversation (highlights): - Miguel Soto (2026-02-11): "Nice design — can you clarify how histograms are merged across pools? Concerned about memory usage at high cardinality." - Ava Chen (2026-02-11): "We use fixed bins (configurable) and only store counts + sample moments; per-tenant histograms are sharded and TTL'd after inactivity to bound memory. Added comments and a benchmark in sim harness." - Priya Nair (2026-02-13): "Need to ensure degrade events are rate-limited to avoid flip-flopping; also add observability that ties degrade events to fallback model choice." - Ava Chen (2026-02-14): "Added a token-bucket rate limiter for degrade events and expanded telemetry with degrade_reason and fallback_model tags." - Liam O'Connor (2026-02-15): "Integration tests look good, but failing flakily under high synthetic variance." - Ava Chen (2026-02-16): "Tuned smoothing window from 30->60s and added jitter in sim to validate. Reran CI and repros are stable."

CI checks and status: - build: passed - unit-tests: passed (coverage +0.4%) - integration-smoke: passed in staging - lint: passed - benchmark-regression: baseline within 1% - e2e-dedicated: passed after stability fix

Edge cases and limitations: - This autoscaler assumes requests report expected output token estimation; for models that perform variable decoding strategies (e.g., sampling with early stop heuristics) observed lengths can still be noisy — the policy uses conservative smoothing. - Per-tenant histogram labels introduce extra cardinality; disabled by default for tenants with <1000 reqs/day. - The degrade limiter is soft: it opts for graceful capacity shedding or fallback to fast variants; we do not unilaterally kill in-flight requests.

Operational notes for SRE: - When enabling for a pool, monitor metrics: seqlen_effective_concurrency, seqlen_bucket_counts, degrade_limiter_events and fallback_model_uses. - Recommended rollout: canary two pools with traffic mirroring enabled, watch for p95 latency regressions and increase window_size_seconds if noisy. - Rollback: switch pool autoscaler config back to "token-rate" and clear degraded_tenants cache.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged into main (merge method: squash). Backported a small hotfix to release/2026-02 for an off-by-one in bucket indexing.

Related work: links to design doc and Linear tickets: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1429/seqlen-aware-autoscaler-design (reference), internal runbook: docs/internal/autoscaling-seqlen.md.

notes_for_release: Opt-in autoscaler. Not enabled by default. Ops: when turning on for a pool, follow canary guidance in runbook. Backported off-by-one bucket indexing fix to release/2026-02.
changelog_entry: Added sequence-length-aware window autoscaler and tenant burst degrade limiter; per-seqlen utilization telemetry for better capacity planning.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: oscillation for highly erratic seq-length workloads. Mitigation: conservative default smoothing, canary rollout, explicit rate limiting of degrade events, and immediate rollback to token-rate policy.
